name: Improper Authorization
principle: The product omits or incorrectly performs an authorization check when an actor accesses a resource or invokes an action. Authenticated users can read, modify, or execute functions beyond their permitted role or object ownership.
detection_signals: handler/controller calls getById(id), find(id), load(id), DisplayPrivateMessage(id), delete(id), update(id) using request parameter without canAccess(user,id) or owner check
admin or privileged endpoint lacks role check such as isAdmin(), hasRole("ADMIN"), @PreAuthorize, @RolesAllowed, or JAAS Subject.doAs policy check
server route relies only on authentication check such as isAuthenticated(), AuthenticateUser(), getUserPrincipal(), or session != null before sensitive action
authorization enforced only in UI code such as disabled button, hidden link, JavaScript role check, or client-side route guard
direct file/resource return via sendFile(), FileInputStream, static file mapping, or download(id/path) without ACL or permission check
database query filters by user-controlled id but not by current user or tenant, e.g. WHERE id = ? instead of WHERE id = ? AND owner_id = ?
Android component exposes sensitive Activity/Service/Receiver with android:exported="true" and no permission attribute
negative_signals: server-side check hasRole/hasAuthority/@PreAuthorize/@RolesAllowed before the privileged method
object-level predicate checks resource.ownerId == currentUser.id or ACL.canRead/currentUser before read/write
database query includes tenant/user constraint from trusted session, e.g. WHERE id = ? AND owner_id = currentUser.id
default-deny middleware/filter/interceptor protects the route and explicit allow rules list required permission
OS or server ACL is set before exposure, e.g. chmod 600, non-public directory, or web server deny rule for sensitive files
Android component uses android:exported="false" or requires a signature-level permission
false_defense_traps: Authentication check alone; knowing who the user is does not prove permission for this resource
RBAC role check alone for same-role data; horizontal authorization needs object ownership or ACL checks
Client-side hiding or disabling controls; direct URL or parameter changes bypass it
SQL injection protection alone; prepared statements do not enforce authorization
Database account permissions alone; business records still need per-user or per-tenant authorization
verification_focus: Does every sensitive server-side resource/action verify that the authenticated actor has permission for that exact operation and object?

consequence_chains.trigger: sensitive endpoint or resource has no authorization check
consequence_chains.consequence: unauthorized read, write, privilege gain, or command execution

consequence_chains.trigger: authorization check exists but uses wrong role, user, tenant, object, or condition
files or directories are exposed without access restriction
consequence_chains.consequence: external parties read sensitive files or directories

consequence_chains.trigger: critical resource is assigned overly broad permissions
consequence_chains.consequence: unauthorized actors modify or read protected resources

patch_principle: Enforce server-side authorization on every sensitive route, method, page, file, and object access.
Use default-deny RBAC for roles and add object-level owner/tenant/ACL checks for business data.
Use vetted authorization frameworks such as JAAS, @PreAuthorize/@RolesAllowed, or ESAPI Access Control.
Keep authorization decisions based on trusted session identity, not request-supplied user, role, tenant, or owner fields.
Configure OS, server, and application ACLs so sensitive files and components are not publicly accessible.

minimal_examples.safe: Message m = dao.findMessage(id); if (!m.ownerId.equals(currentUser.id)) throw new ForbiddenException(); return m.body;
